If a line passing through the centre of the circle C intersects $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ at ( $-1,2$ ) and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ at ( $3,-6$ ), then the equation of the circle C is

options.D:
$(\mathrm{x}-1)^{2}+(\mathrm{y}-2)^{2}=16$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{L}_{1}: 4 \mathrm{x}-3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{K}_{1}=0 \\
\mathrm{~L}_{2}: 4 \mathrm{x}-3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{K}_{2}=0
\end{array}$$
now
$$\begin{array}{l}
-4-6+\mathrm{K}_{1}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}_{1}=10 \\
12+18+\mathrm{K}_{2}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}_{2}=-30

⇒ Tangent to the circle are
$$\begin{array}{l}
4 x-3 y+10=0 \\

Length of diameter $2 \mathrm{r}=\frac{|10+30|}{5}=8$
$$\Rightarrow r=4$$

Now centre is mid point of A \& B

Equation of circle

questions.text: The value of $\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\cos x} \sin x}{\left(1+\cos ^{2} x\right)\left(\mathrm{e}^{\cos x}+\mathrm{e}^{-\cos x}\right)} d x$ is equal to

options.D:
$\frac{\pi}{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\cos \mathrm{x}} \sin \mathrm{x}}{\left(1+\cos ^{2} \mathrm{x}\right)\left(\mathrm{e}^{\cos \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{e}^{-\cos \mathrm{x}}\right)} \mathrm{dx}$

Use King's property
$$I=\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{e^{-\cos x} \sin x}{\left(1+\cos ^{2} x\right)\left(e^{-\cos x}+e^{\cos x}\right)} d x$$

On adding equation (1) and (2), we get
$$2 I=\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos ^{2} x} d x=2 \int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos ^{2} x} d x$$

On putting $\cos x=t$, we get
$$I=\int_{0}^{1} \frac{d t}{1+t^{2}}=\left(\tan ^{-1} t\right)_{0}^{1}=\frac{\pi}{4}$$

questions.text:
Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{N} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a function such that $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=2 \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y})$ for natural numbers x and y. If $f(1)=2$, then the value of $\alpha$ for which
$$\sum_{k=1}^{10} f(\alpha+k)=\frac{512}{3}\left(2^{20}-1\right)$$
holds, is

options.D:
6

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
f: N \rightarrow R, f(x+y)=2 f(x) f(y) \\
f(1)=2, \\
\sum_{k=1}^{10} f(\alpha+k)=2 f(\alpha) \sum_{k=1}^{10} f(k) \\
=2 f(\alpha)(f(1)+f(2)+\ldots . .+f(10))
\end{array}$$

From (1)
$$\begin{array}{l}
f(2)=2 f^{2}(1)=2^{3} \\
f(3)=2 f(2) f(1)=2^{5}
\end{array}$$
from (2)
$$\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{k=1}^{10} f(\alpha+k)=2\left(2^{2 \alpha-1}\right)\left(2+2^{3}+2^{5}+\ldots .+2^{19}\right) \\
\frac{512}{3}\left(2^{20}-1\right)=2^{2 \alpha}\left(2 \frac{\left(2^{20}-1\right)}{3}\right)
\end{array}$$

Hence $\alpha=4$

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be defined as $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{3}+\mathrm{x}-5$. If $\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})$ is a function such that $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x}))=\mathrm{x}$, $\forall \mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$, then $\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(63)$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$ .

options.D:
$\frac{91}{49}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{3}+\mathrm{x}-5$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=3 \mathrm{x}^{2}+1 \Rightarrow$ increasing function
⇒ invertible
$\Rightarrow \quad g(x)$ is inverse of $f(x)$
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{g}(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))=\mathrm{x}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})) \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=1$
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=63$
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{x}^{3}+\mathrm{x}-5=63$
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{x}=4$
put $\mathrm{x}=4$
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{f}(4)) \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(4)=1$
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(63) \times 49=1 \quad\left\{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(4)=49\right\}$
$\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(63)=\frac{1}{49}$

questions.text: If $\frac{1}{2 \cdot 3^{10}}+\frac{1}{2^{2} \cdot 3^{9}}+\ldots \frac{1}{2^{10} \cdot 3}=\frac{K}{2^{10} \cdot 3^{10}}$, then the remainder when K is divided by 6 is

options.D:
5

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\frac{1}{2 \cdot 3^{10}}+\frac{1}{2^{2} \cdot 3^{9}}+\frac{1}{2^{3} \cdot 3^{8}}+\ldots \ldots+\frac{1}{2^{10} \cdot 3}=\frac{\mathrm{K}}{2^{10} \cdot 3^{10}}$
$\mathrm{K}=2^{9}+2^{8} \cdot 3+2^{7} \cdot 3^{2}+\ldots . .+3^{9}$
$=\frac{2^{9}\left(\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{10}-1\right)}{\frac{3}{2}-1}=3^{10}-2^{10}$
Now,
$$\begin{aligned}
3^{10}-2^{10} & =\left(3^{5}-2^{5}\right)\left(3^{5}+2^{5}\right) \\
& =(211)(275) \\
& =(35 \times 6+1)(45 \times 6+5) \\
& =6 \lambda+5
\end{aligned}$$

Remainder is 5.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{E}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{E}_{2}$ be two events such that the conditional probabilities $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \mid \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$, $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2} \mid \mathrm{E}_{1}\right)=\frac{3}{4}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{8}$. Then:

options.D:
$\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}^{\prime} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right) \cdot \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol.
(A) $\quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right) \cdot \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{6} \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{24} \neq \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)$
(B)
$$\begin{aligned}
P\left(E_{1}^{\prime} \cap E_{2}^{\prime}\right) & =1-P\left(E_{1} \cup E_{2}\right) \\
& =1-\left(P\left(E_{1}\right)+P\left(E_{2}\right)-P\left(E_{1} \cap E_{2}\right)\right) \\
& =1-\left(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{8}\right)=\frac{17}{24}
\end{aligned}$$
$\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}^{\prime}\right) \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{5}{24}$
(C) $\quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}^{\prime}\right)=\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right)-\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{1}{24}$
(D) $\quad \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}^{\prime} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)-\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1} \cap \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{1}{8}$

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{array}\right]$. If M and N are two matrices given by $\mathrm{M}=\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{10} \mathrm{~A}^{2 \mathrm{k}}$ and $\mathrm{N}=\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{10} \mathrm{~A}^{2 \mathrm{k}-1}$ then $\mathrm{MN}^{2}$ is

options.D:
an identify matrix

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)

Sol. $\mathrm{A}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{array}\right]$
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{A}^{2} & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}
0 & -2 \\
2 & 0
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}
0 & -2 \\
2 & 0
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}
-4 & 0 \\
0 & -4
\end{array}\right]=-4 \mathrm{I} \\
\mathrm{~A}^{3} & =-4 \mathrm{~A} \\
\mathrm{~A}^{4} & =(-4 \mathrm{I})(-4 \mathrm{I})=(-4)^{2} \mathrm{I} \\
\mathrm{~A}^{5} & =(-4)^{2} \mathrm{~A}, \quad \mathrm{~A}^{6}=(-4)^{3} \mathrm{I} \\
\mathrm{M} & =\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{10} \mathrm{~A}^{2 \mathrm{k}}=\mathrm{A}^{2}+\mathrm{A}^{4}+\ldots .+\mathrm{A}^{20} \\
& =\left[-4+(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{3}+\ldots .+(-4)^{20}\right] \mathrm{I} \\
& =-4 \lambda \mathrm{I}
\end{aligned}$$

⇒ M is symmetric matrix
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{N} & =\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{10} \mathrm{~A}^{2 \mathrm{k}-1}=\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{A}^{3}+\ldots . .+\mathrm{A}^{19} \\
& =\mathrm{A}\left[1+(-4)+(-4)^{2}+\ldots . .+(-4)^{9}\right] \\
& =\lambda \mathrm{A} \Rightarrow \text { skew symmetric }
\end{aligned}$$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{N}^{2}$ is symmetric matrix
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{MN}^{2}$ is non identity symmetric matrix

questions.text:
Let $\mathrm{g}:(0, \infty) \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a differentiable function such that
$\int\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}(\cos \mathrm{x}-\sin \mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1}+\frac{\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})\left(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1-\mathrm{xe}^{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\left(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1\right)^{2}}\right) \mathrm{dx}=\frac{\mathrm{xg}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}+1}+\mathrm{c}$,
for all $\mathrm{x}>0$, where c is an arbitrary constant.
Then.

options.D:
$\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{g}^{\prime}$ is increasing in $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)

JEE Exam Solution
www.esaral.com
4

Saral
JEE | NEET | Class 8-10 Download eSaral APP

Sol.
$$\int\left(\frac{x(\cos x-\sin x)}{e^{x}+1}+\frac{g(x)\left(e^{x}+1-x e^{x}\right)}{\left(e^{x}+1\right)^{2}}\right) d x=\frac{x g(x)}{e^{x}+1}+c$$

On differentiating both sides w.r.t. x , we get
$$\begin{array}{l}
\left(\frac{x(\cos x-\sin x)}{e^{x}+1}+\frac{g(x)\left(e^{x}+1-x e^{x}\right.}{\left(e^{x}+1\right)^{2}}\right) \\
=\frac{\left(e^{x}+1\right)\left(g(x)+x g^{\prime}(x)\right)-e^{x} \cdot x \cdot g(x)}{\left(e^{x}+1\right)^{2}} \\
\left(e^{x}+1\right) x(\cos x-\sin x)+g(x)\left(e^{x}+1-x e^{x}\right) \\
=\left(e^{x}+1\right)\left(g(x)+x g^{\prime}(x)\right)-e^{x} \cdot x \cdot g(x) \\
\Rightarrow g^{\prime}(x)=\cos x-\sin x \\
\Rightarrow g(x)=\sin x+\cos x+C
\end{array}$$
$\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})$ is increasing in $(0, \pi / 4)$
$$g^{\prime \prime}(x)=-\sin x-\cos x<0$$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ is decreasing function
let $h(x)=g(x)+g^{\prime}(x)=2 \cos x+C$
$$\Rightarrow h^{\prime}(x)=g^{\prime}(x)+g^{\prime \prime}(x)=-2 \sin x<0$$

⇒ h is decreasing
let $\phi(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2 \sin \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$
$$\Rightarrow \phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{g}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=2 \cos \mathrm{x}>0$$
$\Rightarrow \phi$ is increasing
Hence option D is correct.

questions.text:
Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{g}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be two functions defined by $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}+1\right)-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}}+1$ and $\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{1-2 \mathrm{e}^{2 \mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}$. Then, for which of the following range of $\alpha$, the inequality
$$\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{~g}\left(\frac{(\alpha-1)^{2}}{3}\right)\right)>\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{~g}\left(\alpha-\frac{5}{3}\right)\right) \text { holds? }$$

options.D:
$(-1,1)$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)

Sol. $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}+1\right)-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}}+1$
$$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}+1}+\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{x}}>0 \quad \forall \mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$$

⇒ f is strictly increasing
$$\begin{array}{l}
g(x)=\frac{1-2 e^{2 x}}{e^{x}}=e^{-x}-2 e^{x} \\
\Rightarrow g^{\prime}(x)=-\left(2 e^{x}+e^{-x}\right)<0 \quad \forall x \in R
\end{array}$$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}$ is decreasing
Now $\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{g}\left(\frac{(\alpha-1)^{2}}{3}\right)\right)>\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{g}\left(\alpha-\frac{5}{3}\right)\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow g\left(\frac{(\alpha-1)^{2}}{3}\right)>g\left(\alpha-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \frac{(\alpha-1)^{2}}{3}<\alpha-\frac{5}{3} \\
\Rightarrow \alpha^{2}-5 \alpha+6<0 \\
\Rightarrow(\alpha-2)(\alpha-3)<0 \\
\Rightarrow \alpha \in(2,3)
\end{array}$$
